occasions.question: Is this lunch, wherever it came from?

occasions.question: Is this the 3-6pm energy trough, away from home?

occasions.question: Is this an at-home tea or snack between lunch and dinner?

occasions.question: Is this being bought and eaten outside, before dinner?

occasions.question: Is this the main evening meal, however it arrived?

occasions.competes_with: roti-sabzi, rice-dal, khichdi, whatever was cooked, Swiggy or Zomato, the restaurant downstairs, a bhojanalay or mess, takeaway on the way home, a friend's house

occasions.channel: the home kitchen, a delivery app, the eatery on the corner, a friend's kitchen

occasions.question: Is this after 10pm, unplanned, and usually alone?
occasions.moment: after 10pm, unplanned, usually on your own
occasions.competes_with: instant noodles, chips, ice cream, chocolate, leftover mithai, an app order, nothing
occasions.decided_by: what is in the cupboard, what will arrive in ten minutes
occasions.channel: quick commerce, the kitchen cupboard, a late delivery app

occasions.question: Is a drink being had to end the day or help someone sleep?
occasions.moment: a drink that ends the day, for yourself or for someone else
occasions.competes_with: malted milk, plain or haldi doodh, herbal tea, nothing
occasions.decided_by: routine, whether it is for a child, whether it helps sleep
occasions.channel: the kitchen, the monthly grocery order

occasions.question: Is a journey the reason this is being bought or packed?
occasions.moment: a journey — packed for it, or bought because of it
occasions.competes_with: theplas packed from home, station snacks, the airport counter, a highway dhaba, biscuits and namkeen for the bag
occasions.decided_by: portability, shelf life, what the counter has, captive pricing
occasions.channel: packed at home, the station, the airport store, a highway stop

occasions.question: Is food being put out because someone else is in the house?
occasions.moment: putting food out because someone has come over
occasions.competes_with: namkeen, mithai, a chocolate box, cold drinks, tea service, something ordered in for everyone
occasions.decided_by: what looks right in front of a guest, what is in the tin
occasions.channel: the household stock-up, the sweet shop, a delivery app

occasions.question: Is this bought for someone else, because of an occasion?
occasions.moment: buying for someone else because the calendar says so
occasions.competes_with: mithai boxes, dry fruit, chocolate hampers, corporate gift packs
occasions.decided_by: what it says about the giver, price bracket, presentation
occasions.channel: the sweet shop, a supermarket gifting aisle, online hampers

occasions.question: Is there a reason to treat — a result, a promotion, a match?
occasions.moment: a reason to treat, alone or as a group
occasions.competes_with: cake, chocolate, ice cream, eating out, a round for the office, a spread arranged by an employer
occasions.decided_by: the size of the occasion, who is paying, what is shared
occasions.channel: a bakery, a restaurant, a delivery app, the office pantry

occasions.question: Is someone unwell, pregnant, elderly or convalescing?
occasions.moment: food for someone who is unwell, pregnant, elderly or recovering
occasions.competes_with: khichdi, ORS, prescribed nutrition, home remedies, what the doctor said, plain food
occasions.decided_by: what the doctor said, what will stay down, what is gentle
occasions.channel: the kitchen, the pharmacy, a prescription

occasions.question: Is this immediately before or after exercise?
occasions.moment: the window either side of exercise
occasions.competes_with: a whey shake, eggs, a banana, an electrolyte, dal-chawal at home, nothing
occasions.decided_by: protein per serving, timing, what the trainer said
occasions.channel: the gym counter, specialist online, the gym bag

occasions.question: Is this taken on a schedule, whether or not anyone is hungry?
occasions.moment: something taken on a schedule — chosen by them or prescribed
occasions.competes_with: a powder, gummies, a multivitamin, a prescribed tablet, a high-protein drink, "I'd rather just eat properly"
occasions.decided_by: routine, whether it seems to work, cost per day, whether a doctor said so
occasions.channel: a subscription, specialist online, the pharmacy, the kitchen

occasions.question: Is this drunk for thirst rather than as part of a moment?
occasions.moment: drinking for thirst, not as part of anything else
occasions.competes_with: water, buttermilk, coconut water, a cold drink, juice, an electrolyte, nimbu pani
occasions.decided_by: heat, what is cold and nearby, price
occasions.channel: the fridge, a shop counter, a street cart, the water bottle

occasions.question: Is this a purchase for later, by and for several people?
occasions.moment: the weekly or monthly shop — buying for other people too
occasions.competes_with: biscuit packs, namkeen, cereal, staples, whatever the children will actually eat
occasions.decided_by: price per unit, family acceptance, what keeps
occasions.channel: the supermarket, online grocery, the local kirana, quick commerce

grid.alternatives_heading: WHAT USUALLY WINS THESE MOMENTS — nameable, real, and often not bought by the person who eats it:
everyday_alternatives: chai — made at home, or ₹10-₹20 at a stall; the single most common thing in an Indian day and the default in at least four of these moments
Parle-G / Britannia Marie, Good Day, 50-50 — ₹5-₹40 biscuit packs
khaari, rusk, fafda, khakra, dhokla, pakoda, thepla, chakli, murukku — ₹10-₹50, regional and everyday, usually bought loose by weight from a farsan shop or a bakery with no brand and no date on it
jalebi, mithai and the local halwai's sweets — bought by weight, and the thing a wife packs into a lunch tiffin without anybody calling it a treat
canteen samosa, vada pav, aloo patty, momos — ₹10-₹40, hot and immediate
Cadbury Dairy Milk, KitKat, Snickers — ₹10-₹100 impulse chocolate
Maggi and other instant noodles — ₹15-₹30, and the 2am default
Amul buttermilk, Frooti, Sprite, Coke, fresh lime — ₹10-₹40 cold drinks
filter coffee, instant coffee, a ₹250 cafe frappe at the other end
a banana or an apple from the fruit cart — ₹10-₹20
home food someone else cooked or packed — a tiffin, a thali, a spread the employer laid on; costs the eater nothing and still wins the moment
nothing at all — waiting it out until the next meal

raw.label: loyalist_tapri_chai_break
raw.l1_context: The 4pm walk to the stall outside started as a smoke break with two others and stayed after the smoking stopped; it is the break, not the drink.
raw.l2_category: Cutting chai at the same stall six days a week, ₹12-₹15, sometimes a Parle-G or a samosa with it; pays weekly on a running tab.
raw.l3_knowledge: Knows which stall boils the milk properly and what a samosa should cost. Does NOT know what a protein bar contains or costs. Does NOT know Blinkit sells anything at this hour.
raw.l4_stance: Wants five minutes standing outside with the same two people. Rejects anything that turns the break into a purchase decision or a solo desk snack.
raw.l5_behavior: Refused a colleague's offered Yogabar bar last Tuesday and walked down for chai and a samosa at the usual stall instead.

dispositions.label: skeptic_protein_on_everything
dispositions.anchor:
Bought into the healthy-snack pitch once during a fitness phase, ate two bars, found the rest still in the cupboard months later past date.

Now buys almost nothing in the afternoon; if anything, namkeen by weight from the farsan shop or whatever is in the tin at home.

Knows the word protein is now on chips, biscuits and water. Does NOT know whether the number on any pack is verified, and does NOT know what these bars are actually made of beyond 'dates and something'.

Wants food that is food. Rejects paying near a hundred rupees for a wrapped bar when the same money is a proper plate at the stall downstairs.

Threw out an unopened half-box of Yogabar bars bought on Amazon during a January gym phase; went back to bhujia with the afternoon chai.

dispositions.label: purist_home_food_only_afternoon
dispositions.anchor:
Grew up on food cooked at home twice a day; a stomach infection after eating outside once turned a preference into a rule that nothing packaged enters the afternoon.

Buys almost nothing in the afternoon; carries roasted chana or last night's thepla, and drinks chai made at home before leaving.

Knows biscuits and namkeen by sight and price at the kirana. Does NOT know what a protein bar contains or costs. Does NOT know Blinkit or Zepto sell food at all.

Wants food that was cooked by a person, not sealed in a factory. Rejects anything with a shelf life longer than a week, however healthy the pack claims.

Turned down a colleague's Yogabar at the counter last week and ate the guava brought from the fruit cart instead.

dispositions.label: pragmatist_whatever_fills_till_dinner
dispositions.anchor:
Dinner is at ten and lunch was at one; the afternoon gap is a hunger problem, not a health project, and it gets solved with whatever is at the counter.

Buys most working days at the shop by the gate, ten to twenty rupees, chosen on what actually stops the hunger till dinner.

Knows exactly which packs feel filling and which vanish in three bites. Does NOT know what 'whey' is. Does NOT read anything on the back of a pack.

Wants to not be hungry at six. Rejects small expensive packs that leave the stomach the same — the price is fine only if it ends the hunger.

Bought a ₹18 Dairy Milk on Tuesday, was hungry again by five, went back for a vada pav from the cart.

dispositions.label: gifter_office_round_afternoon
dispositions.anchor:
Being the one who feeds the group in the dead part of the afternoon bought a place in it; the buying is the point and the eating barely registers.

Orders for six or seven people two or three times a month, hundred to four hundred rupees, always a shareable format nobody has to explain.

Knows which flavours the team will fight over and what arrives fastest. Does NOT know what any of it costs per gram. Does NOT know which brands are considered healthy.

Wants something that opens on a desk and gets passed around. Rejects single-serve health bars — one bar for one person makes it a private thing, not a round.

Got a KitKat multipack and a big Lay's on Instamart at four when a colleague's result came through, opened both on the shared table.
